esco_onet.name: ESCO-O*NET Crosswalk (Occupations), EC ESCO Secretariat + US DOL/ETA, v1 Sep-2022
esco_onet.license: EC reuse (Decision 2011/833/EU), commercial use allowed with attribution

ilo.name: ILO WP140 Gmyrek et al. (2025) GenAI task scores, ISCO-08

noc_soc.name: StatCan NOC 2016 V1.3 to SOC 2018 (US) correspondence

noc16_21.name: StatCan NOC 2016 V1.3 to NOC 2021 V1.0 correspondence

method.dedupe: ESCO skill URI identity; then identical normalized text (lowercase, punctuation/stopwords removed, light suffix stemming, sorted token set); then token-set Jaccard >= 0.6 within the occupation (knowledge items only merge by URI/text); then a second pass folds true cross-source duplicates (symmetric -ing/-e/plural stemming, Jaccard >= 0.75, at most 2 differing tokens, never two rows of the same source or two distinct ESCO skills) into their best match. Deterministic and offline; no embeddings.
method.crosswalk_weights: ESCO match type: exact 1.0, close 0.8, narrow 0.6, broad 0.5 (relatedMatch excluded: not validated by US DOL); ESCO optional skills x0.5. ILO/OaSIS: 1/n of mapped ISCO groups / NOC units. ISCO groups = BLS SOC2010->ISCO-08 list, intersected with the ISCO groups of the ESCO occupations mapped to this O*NET code when that intersection is non-empty. NICE: 0.5, curated title mapping (no official SOC crosswalk). O*NET tasks: Anthropic time share / the occupation max (equal weights when missing).
method.exposure: Only published scores. AI direct: Anthropic Economic Index task penetration (O*NET tasks) and ILO WP140 2025 task score (ISCO tasks). Robotics direct: Anthropic robot exposure tier E0-E3 on O*NET tasks (score = tier/3). Others inherit from the most lexically similar directly-scored statement in the same occupation when Jaccard >= 0.34 (basis "transferred", donor and similarity recorded); otherwise null. Calibration: each AI source -> its own percentile (share of that source's statements scoring strictly lower, so a zero score stays 0; statements with both: mean).
method.blend_full: See scripts/blend.js and docs/BLEND_COMPARISON.md: every available measure as a percentile across occupations, grouped into independent families (AI: observed use, rated LLM exposure, ability-based, ILO tasks, market targeting; robotics: Anthropic robot, O*NET degree of automation, deployed robots); family = mean of available members; blend = mean of available families (missing re-weighted, never zero).
method.blend_v1_superseded: AI: unweighted mean of two independent task-level sources, each weight-averaged over its directly-scored statements: O*NET tasks (Anthropic penetration percentile, time-share weights) and ISCO-08 tasks (ILO 2025 percentile, 1/n ISCO weights). ESCO/OaSIS/NICE statements carry transferred scores for display but do not vote (no published task score of their own). Robotics: only O*NET tasks carry a published robot tier, so the robotics blend equals the O*NET task mean. Primary since Oct 21, 2026 (Drew approved).
